content: The references provided are a collection of studies and clinical trials that investigate the efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness of various treatments for bone metastases and associated complications in cancer patients. These studies focus on the use of bisphosphonates (such as clodronate, pamidronate, ibandronate, and zoledronic acid) and denosumab, a RANK ligand inhibitor, in managing skeletal-related events (SREs), bone pain, and quality of life in patients with metastatic bone disease from cancers such as breast cancer, prostate cancer, lung cancer, and others. 1. Broom RJ et al. (2015): This randomized phase II trial evaluated the combination of everolimus and zoledronic acid in patients with renal cell carcinoma and bone metastases. The study aimed to assess the efficacy of this combination as a first-line treatment. 2. Dearnaley DP et al. (2003): A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial investigated the use of oral sodium clodronate in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The trial, known as the MRC PR05 Trial, assessed the impact of clodronate on disease progression and skeletal complications. 3. Diel I et al. (2004): This study demonstrated that long-term treatment with the bisphosphonate ibandronate improved the quality of life in patients with metastatic bone disease due to breast cancer. 4. Elomaa I et al. (1992): A controlled study examined the effect of oral clodronate on bone pain in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The findings highlighted its potential in pain management. 5. Ernst DS et al. (1997): A randomized, controlled trial assessed the use of intravenous clodronate in patients with metastatic bone disease and pain, showing its efficacy in pain relief. 6. Ernst DS et al. (1992): A double-blind, crossover trial evaluated intravenous clodronate for metastatic bone pain, confirming its effectiveness in reducing pain symptoms. 7. Ernst DS et al. (2003): This randomized, double-blind, controlled trial compared mitoxantrone/prednisone with clodronate versus mitoxantrone/prednisone with placebo in patients with hormone-refractory prostate cancer and pain, demonstrating the benefits of clodronate in this setting. 8. Heras P et al. (2009): The efficacy of ibandronate in treating skeletal events in patients with metastatic breast cancer was evaluated, showing significant benefits in reducing skeletal complications. 9. Hortobagyi GN et al. (1996): This study demonstrated that pamidronate effectively reduced skeletal complications in patients with breast cancer and lytic bone metastases, as part of the Aredia Breast Cancer Study Group Protocol 19. 10. James N et al. (2016): The TRAPEZE trial assessed the clinical and cost-effectiveness of chemotherapy combined with zoledronic acid, strontium-89, or both in men with bony metastatic castration-refractory prostate cancer. 11. Kanis JA et al. (1996): This study showed that clodronate decreased the frequency of skeletal metastases in women with breast cancer, highlighting its preventive potential. 12. Kohno N et al. (2005): A randomized, placebo-controlled trial in Japanese women with bone metastases from breast cancer demonstrated that zoledronic acid significantly reduced skeletal complications compared to placebo. 13. Kristensen B et al. (1999): A randomized study evaluated oral clodronate in breast cancer patients with bone metastases, confirming its efficacy in managing skeletal-related events. 14. Kylmala T et al. (1993): This controlled trial by the Finnish Prostate Cancer Group assessed the effect of oral clodronate on skeletal metastases using type 1 collagen metabolites as biomarkers. 15. Lipton A et al. (2000): Long-term follow-up of two randomized, placebo-controlled trials showed that pamidronate prevents skeletal complications and provides effective palliative treatment in women with breast carcinoma and osteolytic bone metastases. 16. Martoni A et al. (1991): A controlled clinical study investigated the use of dichloromethylene diphosphonate in patients with breast carcinoma metastasizing to the skeleton, demonstrating its therapeutic benefits. 17. Meulenbeld H et al. (2012): The Netherlands Prostate Study (NePro) evaluated docetaxel with or without risedronate in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, showing the potential benefits of combining these treatments. 18. Murakami H et al. (2014): A phase II study by the West Japan Oncology Group assessed zoledronic acid combined with docetaxel for non-small-cell lung cancer, demonstrating its efficacy in managing bone metastases. 19. O’Rourke N et al. (1995): A double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-response trial of oral clodronate in patients with bone metastases confirmed its effectiveness in reducing skeletal complications. 20. Pan Y et al. (2014): This study compared docetaxel with or without zoledronic acid in castration-resistant prostate cancer, showing the added benefits of zoledronic acid in managing bone metastases. 21. Paterson AH et al. (1993): A double-blind controlled trial of oral clodronate in patients with bone metastases from breast cancer demonstrated its efficacy in reducing skeletal-related events. 22. Piga A et al. (1998): A double-blind randomized study evaluated oral clodronate in treating bone metastases from tumors poorly responsive to chemotherapy, confirming its therapeutic role. 23. Robertson AG et al. (1995): A double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed the effect of oral clodronate on metastatic bone pain, showing significant pain relief. 24. Rosen LS et al. (2003): A phase III, double-blind, randomized trial compared zoledronic acid versus placebo in treating skeletal metastases in lung cancer and other solid tumors, demonstrating the superiority of zoledronic acid. 25. Siris ES et al. (1983): This study evaluated the effects of dichloromethylene diphosphonate in women with breast carcinoma metastatic to the skeleton, showing its efficacy in managing skeletal complications. 26. Small EJ et al. (2003): A combined analysis of two multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled studies of pamidronate disodium for palliating bone pain in men with metastatic prostate cancer confirmed its effectiveness. 27. Smith J Jr. (1989): A randomized, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated sodium etidronate for palliating painful bone metastases from prostate cancer, showing significant pain relief. 28. Smith MR et al. (2014): The CALGB 90202 trial assessed early zoledronic acid in men with castration-sensitive prostate cancer and bone metastases, demonstrating its benefits in delaying skeletal complications. 29. Theriault RL et al. (1999): A randomized, placebo-controlled trial showed that pamidronate reduces skeletal morbidity in women with advanced breast cancer and lytic bone lesions. 30. Tripathy D et al. (2004): A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated oral ibandronate for treating metastatic bone disease in breast cancer, confirming its efficacy and safety. 31. Tubiana-Hulin M et al. (2001): A double-blinded controlled study compared clodronate versus placebo in patients with breast cancer bone metastases, showing significant benefits of clodronate. 32. Ueno S et al. (2013): The ZABTON-PC study evaluated the efficacy of combined androgen blockade with zoledronic acid in prostate cancer with bone metastasis, demonstrating improved outcomes. 33. van Holten-Verzantvoort AT et al. (1987): Long-term bisphosphonate (APD) treatment reduced morbidity from skeletal metastases in breast cancer patients. 34. van Holten-Verzantvoort AT et al. (1993): Palliative pamidronate treatment in patients with bone metastases from breast cancer showed significant benefits in managing skeletal complications. 35. Vinholes J et al. (1997): A double-blind randomized trial of pamidronate for metastatic bone disease demonstrated relationships between biochemical and symptomatic responses. 36. Wang Y et al. (2013): This study evaluated the clinical significance of zoledronic acid and strontium-89 in patients with asymptomatic bone metastases from non-small-cell lung cancer. 37. Zaghloul MS et al. (2010): A prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of zoledronic acid in bony metastatic bladder cancer demonstrated its efficacy in reducing skeletal complications. 38. Zarogoulidis K et al. (2009): The impact of zoledronic acid therapy on the survival of lung cancer patients with bone metastasis was evaluated, showing improved outcomes. 39. Rosen L et al. (2004): Zoledronic acid was found to be superior to pamidronate for treating bone metastases in breast carcinoma patients with at least one osteolytic lesion. 40. Body J et al. (2007): Oral ibandronate was shown to be as effective as intravenous zoledronic acid in reducing bone turnover markers in women with breast cancer and bone metastases. 41. Francini F et al. (2011): A study compared the effects of intravenous zoledronic acid and oral ibandronate on early changes in bone turnover markers in patients with bone metastases from non-small-cell lung cancer. 42. Choudhury KB et al. (2011): A randomized controlled trial compared the efficacy of bisphosphonates in managing painful bone metastasis, confirming their role in pain relief. 43. Wang F et al. (2013): A comparison between zoledronic acid and clodronate in treating prostate cancer patients with bone metastases showed the superiority of zoledronic acid. 44. Barrett-Lee P et al. (2014): A randomized, open-label, non-inferiority phase 3 trial compared oral ibandronic acid versus intravenous zoledronic acid in treating bone metastases from breast cancer. 45. von Au A et al. (2016): A randomized, open-label, non-inferiority phase III trial compared intravenous pamidronate versus oral and intravenous clodronate in bone metastatic breast cancer. 46. Toussaint ND et al. (2009): This study reviewed the use of bisphosphonates in chronic kidney disease, balancing potential benefits and adverse effects on bone and soft tissue. 47. Botteman M et al. (2006): A cost-effectiveness analysis of bisphosphonates in managing breast cancer patients with bone metastases was conducted. 48. Fleurence RL et al. (2007): A structured review of the cost-effectiveness of bisphosphonates for preventing and treating osteoporosis was performed. 49. Lippuner K et al. (2011): A review of the cost-effectiveness of bisphosphonates in treating postmenopausal osteoporosis in Switzerland was conducted. 50. Sopata M et al. (2015): A study evaluated the efficacy and safety of tanezumab in treating pain from bone metastases. 51. Body JJ et al. (2006): A study investigated the biological receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand inhibitor, denosumab, in patients with multiple myeloma or bone metastases from breast cancer. 52. Lipton A et al. (2008): Extended efficacy and safety of denosumab in breast cancer patients with bone metastases not receiving prior bisphosphonate therapy were demonstrated. 53. Fizazi K et al. (2009): A randomized phase II trial of denosumab in patients with bone metastases from prostate cancer, breast cancer, or other neoplasms after intravenous bisphosphonates was conducted. 54. Stopeck AT et al. (2010): A randomized, double-blind study compared denosumab with zoledronic acid for treating bone metastases in advanced breast cancer patients. 55. Henry DH et al. (2011): A randomized, double-blind study compared denosumab versus zoledronic acid in treating bone metastases in patients with advanced cancer (excluding breast and prostate cancer) or multiple myeloma. 56. Fizazi K et al. (2011): A randomized, double-blind study compared denosumab versus zoledronic acid for treating bone metastases in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer. 57. Martin M et al. (2012): A randomized phase III trial compared denosumab versus zoledronic acid in advanced breast cancer, focusing on bone-related complications and quality of life. 58. Cleeland CS et al. (2012): Pain outcomes in advanced breast cancer patients with bone metastases were evaluated in a randomized, double-blind study of denosumab versus zoledronic acid.
